maria (AE): Hey team, Acme POC is failing when they POST a giant examples array to /v1/infer — getting 413 Request Entity Too Large. Can we troubleshoot?
ellie (SE): Do we have the raw request size and an example of the payload shape? Are they sending one giant JSON with 10k rows?
maria (AE): Yup. They said ~10k small records, each ~1k chars so the JSON payload is ~10MB. They assumed our 32k-token model would accept it as one context.
kai (runtime eng): We have an 8MB ingress limit on hosted endpoints by default to protect memory and sockets. I pulled the ingress logs: 
```
ingress: reject: body_size=12.4MB > max_body=8MB
http: 413 returned to client acme-demo
```
ellie (SE): OK. Options: (A) ask them to stream / chunk on the client with our SDK helper that uploads smaller chunks and assembles server-side, (B) use a pointer pattern — upload full payload to customer S3 and send a secure pointer for us to fetch, (C) for POC temporarily increase body limit for their org. Which is feasible this week?
jordan (sales): Customer cannot use presigned external URLs due to their security policy (no outbound presigned blobs). Also they asked whether splitting into many requests will increase cost — need a clear answer before we propose workarounds.
kai (runtime eng): Technical cost note: billing is per-token processed. If you split into N separate inference calls and repeat a long system or instruction prompt each time, you pay that prompt N times. If you pre-compose the entire context once (pointer pattern) and do a single inference, it's cheaper from total system-token overhead POV. Also repeated requests add more request/response overhead but not necessarily linearly more token compute if you avoid duplicating prompts.
ellie (SE): Streaming SDK approach can avoid re-sending system tokens for each chunk by doing incremental generation with a kept session/KV cache, but that requires client changes. For customers who cannot change infra or allow external storage, we can do a temporary host-side workaround.
maria (AE): Can EngInfra spike a temporary body increase for the org for the POC? They want the demo this week.
kai (runtime eng): I can open an internal ticket to enable a scoped increase (e.g., 16MB) for the customer's org id for 7 days. Need EngInfra + Security signoff. I'll paste the logs and risk notes.
maria (AE): Please do. Also they asked about pricing: if we enable a larger single request, do they get charged differently?
kai (runtime eng): No special pricing change for larger body. It's still per-token. Caveat: very large contexts may trigger slower generation and more GPU time for longer KV caches — that affects cost indirectly. For sustained high-volume big-context workloads we should recommend Dedicated or Private deployments (predictable throughput + config to allow larger request bodies).
jordan (sales): Noted — will surface Dedicated as an option during renewal talks. For immediate demo, we just need the POC to run.
deploy-bot: ticket INC-2026 created: "increase hosted body limit for acme-org (P0 POC)" assigned to eng-infra.
ellie (SE): Quick engineering workaround we can demo today: compress the payload on the client (gzip) and set Content-Encoding: gzip. Our ingress accepts gzip and will decompress, but you still need the post-decompress size within limits. It's hit/miss and fragile. Better to use chunked upload + server assemble, or pointer pattern for reliability.
maria (AE): Security team insists no external presigns. If pointer pattern is required, they prefer an internal S3 we can access from our side (or a Private deployment). I'll loop security in.
kai (runtime eng): Action items: I will 1) open the EngInfra ticket to enable a temporary increase for acme-org, 2) document the pointer vs chunking tradeoffs and the pricing implications, 3) put together a small SDK sample showing uploadChunks + assemble for their client.
ellie (SE): I'll prepare a one-pager for the customer with three options (client chunk + session, internal pointer fetch, temporary hosted increase) + cost notes.
maria (AE): Thanks. Can we get the temporary increase by EOD tomorrow? They want to demo Friday.
kai (runtime eng): I'll push for it and post updates here. :thumbsup:
ellie (SE): For the record, long-term solution is Dedicated/Private or storing huge contexts in a data store and sending pointers — it's more scalable and avoids edge ingress limits.
maria (AE): Great. Looping in security now. cc @security on the no-presign constraint.
